questions.question: What is the term used to describe the ability of the Constitution to adapt and grow over time to meet the changing needs of society?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flexible**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** is the supreme law of India. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country in the world.
 
• The Constitution of India is based on the Government of India Act 1935, but it also incorporates ideas from various other constitutions, such as the British, American, Irish, and Canadian constitutions.
 
• The Constitution of India establishes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.
 
• It guarantees fundamental rights to all citizens, including the right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, and the right to life and personal liberty. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
• It also provides for directive principles of state policy, which are guidelines for the state to follow in formulating its policies.
 
• The Constitution of India divides power between the central government and the state governments.
 
• It establishes a bicameral parliament, consisting of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• The Constitution of India provides for an independent judiciary to interpret the law and uphold the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India is a living document that has been amended several times to keep pace with the changing needs of the country.

questions.question: How many vertical columns are present in the modern periodic table?

• Modern Periodic Table has 18 Groups and 7 Periods.
 
• It has 118 Elements.
 
• Each of the tables has a vertical row is called group. Elements in groups have similar chemical and physical properties because they have the same number of outer electrons.
 
• Each of the tables has horizontal rows is called periods. During a period, a gradual change in chemical properties occurs from one element to another.
 
• The elements are arranged in the modern periodic table on the basis of Mosely law, which states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are the periodic function of their atomic number.
 
• The Structure of it is like a bird Grid.
 
• The Modern Periodic table is used to organize all the known elements.
 
• Advantages of Modern Periodic Table:- 
 
 
• It is easier to remember the properties of an element if its position in the periodic table is known.

questions.question: _______ is a famous Indian folk dance, which is conducted during the Bihu festival in Assam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**Bihu Dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bihu dance is an Indigenous folk dance of the Indian state of Assam.
 
• This dance is usually performed by young men and women.
 
• The dancing style is characterized by brisk steps and rapid hard movements.
 
• In this folk dance, the traditional costumes of dancers are colourful and centred around the red colour theme.
 
• The earliest depiction of Bihu dance is found in the 9th Century Sculptures.
 
• This dance is mainly found in the Tezpur and Darrang districts of Assam.
 
• It is mentioned in the inscriptions of the 14th Century, Chutia and Laxminarayan as well.
 
• Bihu dance is performed outdoors, in fields, groves, etc.
 
• This folk dance takes its name from the Bohag Bihu festival.
 
• Bohag Bihu festival is celebrated as New year in Assam.

 [IMAGE: https://www.gosahin.com/go/p/e/1541270108_Bihu-Dance-Form3.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhortal Dance:** This folk dance form of Assam is performed by the Mishing tribe. It is characterized by its energetic movements and the use of traditional musical instruments like the dhol and the bhortal. The dance is often performed during festivals and cultural events.
 
• **Bagurumba Dance:** Originating from Assam, this dance is performed by the Bodo community. It is a vibrant and colorful dance form that celebrates the arrival of monsoon. The dancers wear traditional attire and perform graceful movements to the rhythm of the dhol and the taal.
 
• **Bardo Chham:** This masked dance-drama is a significant cultural tradition of Sikkim. It is performed by the Bhutia community during festivals and religious ceremonies. The dancers wear elaborate masks and costumes representing various deities and mythical creatures. The dance is believed to ward off evil spirits and bring good fortune.

questions.question: In the First seven five-year plan. in India trade was characterized by what is commonly called an _______ strategy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**inward looking trade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the first seven five-year plans, India adopted an inward-looking trade strategy, focusing on self-reliance and import substitution.
 
• This strategy emphasized the development of domestic industries and reduced dependence on foreign goods.
 
• Policies under this strategy included high tariffs, import restrictions, and the promotion of domestic production.
 
• The aim was to protect nascent industries from international competition and build a robust industrial base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inward Looking Trade Strategy**

 
 
• This strategy involves focusing on the domestic market and limiting foreign competition to protect local industries.
 
• It is often implemented through tariffs, import quotas, and subsidies for domestic industries.
 
• The goal is to develop self-sufficiency and reduce dependency on international trade.
 
• While it can help build local industries, it can also lead to inefficiencies and higher costs due to lack of competition.
 
 
 
• **Import Substitution**
 
 
• Import substitution is an economic policy aimed at replacing foreign imports with domestic production.
 
• This policy is often associated with inward-looking trade strategies and protectionism.
 
• The objective is to reduce foreign dependency and foster local industry growth.
 
• Critics argue that it can lead to economic inefficiency and reduced international trade benefits.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**
 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized economic and social growth initiatives, first launched in 1951.
 
• The plans aimed at structured and balanced development across various sectors.
 
• The First Plan focused on agriculture, while subsequent plans included industrialization, infrastructure, and social services.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating and overseeing these plans until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
 
 
• **Tariffs and Import Restrictions**
 
 
• Tariffs are taxes imposed on imported goods to make them more expensive compared to domestic products.
 
• Import restrictions include quotas and bans that limit the amount or type of goods that can be imported.
 
• These tools are used to protect domestic industries from foreign competition and encourage local production.
 
• However, they can also lead to trade disputes and retaliation from other countries.

questions.question: _______ unveiled a 12 feet high statue of the father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi and a 'Gandhi Vatika' at Gandhi Darshan in New Delhi in September 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India is the ceremonial head of state of India and the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The current President of India, as of September 2023, is Droupadi Murmu.
 
• The President of India plays a significant role in various national events and ceremonies, including inaugurations and unveilings.
 
• On September 2023, the President of India unveiled a 12 feet high statue of Mahatma Gandhi and inaugurated a 'Gandhi Vatika' at Gandhi Darshan in New Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**

 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, commonly known as Mahatma Gandhi, was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist.
 
• He led the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule, employing nonviolent civil disobedience.
 
• Gandhi's vision of an independent India was based on religious pluralism and non-violence.
 
• He is known as the "Father of the Nation" in India and is commemorated on October 2nd, which is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Darshan**
 
 
• Gandhi Darshan is a museum dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi, located in Rajghat, New Delhi.
 
• It was established in 1969 during the commemoration of the centenary of Mahatma Gandhi's birth.
 
• The museum houses various articles, pictures, and memorabilia related to Gandhi's life and works.
 
• Gandhi Darshan is a venue for various educational and cultural programs that promote Gandhian values and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President of India**
 
 
• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament, as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President's primary duties include safeguarding the Constitution, representing India in international forums, and exercising powers related to legislation, appointments, and emergencies.
 
• Though the President's role is largely ceremonial, they possess significant constitutional powers and responsibilities.

questions.question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Arms Act was passed in the year **1878**.
 
• This act was enforced during the period of British rule in India.
 
• The primary objective of the Arms Act of 1878 was to disarm the Indian population and ensure British control.
 
• The act prohibited Indians from possessing firearms without a license and was a significant move to curb any rebellion against the British regime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arms Act, 1878:**

 
 
• The Arms Act, 1878 was enacted by the British Parliament to disarm the Indian population.
 
• Under this act, no Indian could possess firearms without a valid license, making it difficult for Indians to acquire weapons.
 
• The act was specifically designed to prevent any potential uprising or rebellion against the British colonial rule.
 
• This act remained in force until it was repealed and replaced by the Arms Act of 1959 after India gained independence.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Society:**
 
 
• The Arms Act of 1878 had a significant impact on Indian society by curtailing the ability of Indians to defend themselves.
 
• It was seen as a measure to maintain British dominance and suppress any form of resistance or insurgency.
 
• Many Indians were prosecuted under this act for illegal possession of arms, leading to widespread resentment against the British authorities.
 
• The act was one of the many repressive laws imposed by the British to control and subjugate the Indian population.
 
 
 
• **Repeal and Subsequent Legislation:**
 
 
• After India gained independence in 1947, there was a need to revise the existing laws to reflect the new democratic principles.
 
• The Arms Act of 1878 was repealed and replaced by the Arms Act of 1959, which is still in force today.
 
• The new act aimed to regulate the acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, transportation, import, and export of arms and ammunition in India.
 
• The Arms Act of 1959 was designed to ensure that arms are only held by individuals who have a valid reason and are capable of handling them responsibly.

questions.question: In June 2023, The Ministry of _______ recently announced that the Gandhi Peace Prize for 2021 will be conferred upon Gita Press, Gorakhpur.

__
 
• The Ministry of Culture is responsible for the preservation and promotion of art and culture in India.
 
• The Gandhi Peace Prize is an annual award instituted by the Government of India to honor individuals and institutions for their contributions towards social, economic, and political transformation through non-violence and other Gandhian methods.
 
• Gita Press, Gorakhpur is one of the world's largest publishers of Hindu religious texts.
 
• The Gandhi Peace Prize includes a cash award of Rs. 1 crore, a citation, a plaque, and an exquisite traditional handicraft/handloom item.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhi Peace Prize**

• The prize honors those who have made significant contributions to social, economic, and political transformation through non-violence and other Gandhian methods.
 
• It is open to all individuals regardless of nationality, race, creed, or gender.

• Founded in 1923 by Jaya Dayal Goyandka and Ghanshyam Das Jalan in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It specializes in publishing Hindu religious texts including the Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana, and Upanishads.
 
• The press has played a significant role in the dissemination of Hindu philosophy and literature.
 
• Gita Press publications are known for their affordable pricing, making religious texts accessible to a wider audience.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture**
 
 
• The Ministry is tasked with the preservation and promotion of cultural heritage, art, and culture.
 
• It oversees various cultural institutions including museums, libraries, and the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• The Ministry also organizes cultural events and festivals to promote Indian culture both domestically and internationally.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in safeguarding intangible cultural heritage and promoting cultural diversity.

questions.question: Around which of the following year did the Green Revolution begin in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1966**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began around **1966**.
 
• It was initiated by introducing high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially for wheat and rice.
 
• The Green Revolution aimed at transforming India's agricultural sector to increase food production and achieve self-sufficiency.
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is often referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" due to his significant contributions to the movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s.
 
• It began in Mexico and spread globally, significantly impacting countries like India and Pakistan.
 
• The main focus was on the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• This revolution led to a substantial increase in crop production, particularly in wheat and rice.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**
 
 
• HYV seeds are genetically engineered seeds designed to produce more grains per plant.
 
• These seeds are more responsive to fertilizers and irrigation, thereby significantly boosting agricultural output.
 
• However, they often require more inputs like water and chemical fertilizers, which can have environmental impacts.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution helped India transform from a food-deficient country to one that is self-sufficient in food production.
 
• It played a crucial role in reducing hunger and poverty in India, especially in the 1970s and 1980s.
 
• However, it also led to environmental issues such as soil degradation, groundwater depletion, and chemical pollution.
 
 
 
• **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:**
 
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is an Indian geneticist and international administrator renowned for his role in India's Green Revolution.
 
• His efforts in the development and promotion of high-yielding variety seeds were instrumental in making India self-sufficient in food production.
 
• He has received numerous awards for his work, including the first World Food Prize in 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In India within the legislative branch are the _______ houses of parliament.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Parliament of India consists of two houses, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house, and it represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house, and it represents the people of India directly.
 
• Both houses play a critical role in the legislative process, including law-making, budget approval, and discussions on national issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories, using a single transferable vote system.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha envisaged by the Constitution is 552, which includes up to 530 members to represent the States, up to 20 members to represent the Union Territories, and not more than two members of the Anglo-Indian Community to be nominated by the President.
 
• The Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution, and its term is five years unless sooner dissolved.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is its presiding officer and is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Committees**
 
 
• There are several types of committees in the Indian Parliament, including Standing Committees, Ad hoc Committees, and Joint Committees.
 
• These committees play a vital role in the detailed scrutiny of legislation, budget proposals, and other parliamentary business.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Procedure**
 
 
• A bill can be introduced in either house of Parliament, and it must be passed by both houses and receive the President's assent to become law.
 
• There are different types of bills, such as ordinary bills, money bills, and constitutional amendment bills, each with its specific procedure for passage.

questions.question: Crossover Dribble is mainly associated with _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A crossover dribble is a fundamental move in **basketball**.
 
• This move involves switching the ball rapidly from one hand to the other to change direction.
 
• The crossover dribble is used to evade defenders and create scoring opportunities.
 
• Famous basketball players known for their crossover dribble include Allen Iverson and Kyrie Irving.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basketball**

 
 
• Basketball is a team sport where two teams, typically of five players each, oppose one another on a rectangular court, competing to shoot a basketball through the opponent's hoop.
 
• It was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.
 
• The game is played in four quarters of 10 (international) or 12 minutes (NBA).
 
• Popular basketball leagues include the NBA (National Basketball Association) in the USA and the EuroLeague in Europe.
 
 
 
• **Key Basketball Terminologies**
 
 
• **Dribbling:** The act of bouncing the ball continuously with one hand while moving in any direction.
 
• **Shooting:** The action of attempting to score points by throwing the ball through the basket.
 
• **Rebounding:** The act of recovering the ball after a missed shot attempt.
 
• **Assists:** A pass to a teammate that directly leads to a score.
 
• **Defense:** The action of preventing the opposing team from scoring, including blocking shots and stealing the ball.
 
 
 
• **Famous Basketball Players**
 
 
• **Michael Jordan:** Widely considered the greatest basketball player of all time, known for his scoring ability and competitive spirit.
 
• **LeBron James:** A versatile player known for his passing, scoring, and leadership on the court.
 
• **Kobe Bryant:** Renowned for his scoring ability, work ethic, and five NBA championships with the Los Angeles Lakers.
 
• **Stephen Curry:** Revolutionized the game with his exceptional three-point shooting ability.

questions.question: Till 1993-94, the poverty line in India was based on URP data. What does 'URP' stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform Reference Period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Uniform Reference Period" (URP) is used in the context of poverty estimation and data collection methodologies in India.
 
• URP refers to a specific period of time for which data on consumption, income, or other economic indicators are collected uniformly.
 
• In the context of poverty estimation in India, URP data refers to data collected for a 30-day recall period for most consumption items.
 
• Till 1993-94, poverty estimates in India were primarily based on URP data, which provided a consistent basis for poverty measurement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usual Reference Period (URP)**

 
 
• URP data refers to the consumption data collected with a 30-day recall period for most items and a 365-day recall period for some specific items like clothing and durables.
 
• It is a traditional method used for estimating poverty and understanding consumption patterns in India.
 
• URP helps in capturing short-term variations and provides a more realistic picture of consumption.
 
 
 
• **Modified Mixed Reference Period (MMRP)**
 
 
• MMRP is another method for data collection, introduced to improve the accuracy of poverty estimates.
 
• Under MMRP, consumption data is collected with a 7-day recall period for some food items, a 30-day recall for other items, and a 365-day recall for clothing, footwear, and durables.
 
• This method aims to reduce recall errors and provide more accurate estimates of consumption and poverty.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Line**
 
 
• The poverty line is the threshold level of income or consumption below which an individual is considered to be living in poverty.
 
• It is determined based on the cost of a minimum required standard of living, which includes basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, education, and healthcare.
 
• In India, the poverty line is periodically updated based on consumption expenditure surveys conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO).

questions.question: Which country hosts the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaysia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an annual international men's field hockey tournament held in Malaysia.
 
• It was established in 1983 to honor Sultan Azlan Shah, who was an avid supporter and promoter of field hockey.
 
• The tournament is organized by the Malaysian Hockey Confederation and typically features top teams from around the world.
 
• Malaysia has hosted the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup since its inception, making it a significant event in the country's sporting calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Field Hockey**

 
 
• Field hockey is a team sport played on grass or artificial turf, where teams aim to score by hitting a ball into the opponent's goal using hockey sticks.
 
• It is a widely played sport, particularly popular in countries like India, Australia, Netherlands, Germany, and Malaysia.
 
• The game is governed internationally by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), which organizes major tournaments like the Hockey World Cup and the Champions Trophy.
 
• Field hockey has been part of the Summer Olympics since 1908 for men and 1980 for women.
 
 
 
• **International Tournaments**
 
 
• Apart from the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, other significant international field hockey tournaments include the FIH Hockey World Cup, the Olympic Games, and the FIH Pro League.
 
• The FIH Hockey World Cup is held every four years and features the best national teams from around the world.
 
• The Olympic Games field hockey competition is one of the sport's most prestigious events, with teams competing for the gold medal.
 
• The FIH Pro League, launched in 2019, is an annual global league where top national teams compete in home and away matches over several months.
 
 
 
• **Sultan Azlan Shah**
 
 
• Sultan Azlan Shah was the ninth Yang di-Pertuan Agong (King) of Malaysia and the 34th Sultan of Perak.
 
• He was a passionate supporter of field hockey and served as President of the Asian Hockey Federation and Vice-President of the International Hockey Federation.
 
• His contributions to the sport were recognized by naming the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup in his honor.
 
• Under his leadership, Malaysian hockey saw significant growth and development, both domestically and internationally.

questions.question: Which of following festivals is associated with Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modhera Dance Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Modhera Dance Festival, also known as Uttarardh Mahotsav, is a prominent cultural event held annually in Gujarat, India.
 
• It takes place at the Sun Temple in Modhera, a historic site that dates back to the 11th century.
 
• The festival celebrates traditional Indian classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and Kuchipudi.
 
• The event aims to promote and preserve India's rich cultural heritage, attracting numerous tourists and art enthusiasts from across the country and beyond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madai Festival**

 
 
• The Madai Festival is a tribal festival celebrated by the Gond community in the state of Chhattisgarh, India.
 
• The festival includes various rituals, traditional dances, and music, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the tribal community.
 
 
 
• **Bastar Dussehera**
 
 
• Bastar Dussehera is a unique and grand festival celebrated in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, India.
 
• This festival, which lasts for 75 days, is dedicated to the local deities and showcases the region's tribal customs and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Mando Festival**
 
 
• The Mando Festival is celebrated in the state of Goa, India.
 
• It is a traditional Goan festival that showcases the Mando, a form of folk music and dance that is an integral part of Goan culture.
